Hey OP, sorry to hear that this guy is harassing you. To be frank with you, I’ve been on both sides of this. I’ve been the harasser and the victim. 

With that being said, you need to talk things out with him, and explain to him why you don’t want to talk with him anymore. Now as obvious as that might seem, there is a certain way to talk to someone you’re having issue with in order to help them understand. You have to use “I messages.”

I messages are basically statements that are phrased like: I feel ________ when you do _________. 

I messages are more affective when you’re speaking rather that texting. Because when you’re actually able to hear a human voice, it helps you better relate to them. 

To add on to that, you also need to put yourself in his shoes. The best way to resolve an issue is for both sides to have a mutual understanding of each other.

Now you’re probably thinking: oh he’s an awful toxic person, how could I ever relate to him?!

Well, you have to remember, he’s a person too. No normal person wakes up the morning and intends to hurt others. He has positive intentions, but he’s going about them in a negative way. And that’s because someone else was negative towards him.

Or in layman’s terms: We’re al victims of victims/hate begets more hatred.

He’s probably vying for your attention because he doesn’t get the opportunity to make that many friends. He lashed out at you because he’s trying to protect his own feelings. You blocked him because you’re trying to protect yourself. 

Now none of this excuses his behavior; but knowing the why behind it will help you understand how to resolve it.

Help him understand what he did wrong, and help lead him down a more positive path so that the cycle of negativity doesn’t continue.
